question: Drug of choice for Treponema Pallidum is?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Treponema pallidum" -> "causative agent of syphilis" -> "Penicillin G recommended by CDC" -> "effective at all stages of syphilis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Treponema pallidum" -> "sensitive to penicillin" -> "Penicillin G disrupts bacterial cell wall synthesis" -> "bactericidal effect" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Treponema pallidum" -> "alternative treatment needed for penicillin allergy" -> "Doxycycline used as alternative" -> "less effective than Penicillin G" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Treponema pallidum" -> "requires antibiotic treatment" -> "Azithromycin used in some cases" -> "potential for resistance" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Treponema pallidum" -> "treated with antibiotics" -> "Tetracycline is a possible alternative" -> "less preferred due to side effects and resistance issues" -> 75%
analysis: Penicillin G is the first-line treatment for Treponema pallidum, the bacterium that causes syphilis. It is highly effective and has been the standard treatment for many years. Other antibiotics like tetracycline, azithromycin, and doxycycline may be used in cases where patients are allergic to penicillin, but they are not the primary drugs of choice.
